claims.text: A machine-learning approach incorporating atomic-scale descriptors of vibrational disorder and bond heterogeneity can identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity more accurately than traditional empirical or first-principles models.
The target materials are stable crystalline high-entropy alloys with equimolar or near-equimolar compositions.
Significant atomic-size mismatch induces local bonding disorder in the target alloys.
The proposed model integrates first-principles vibrational descriptors with microstructural characterization, including local bond variability.
Phonon transport is the dominant heat-conduction mechanism in the alloys under the stated room-temperature conditions.
Local atomic vibrational disorder enhances phonon scattering.
Local bond heterogeneity enhances phonon scattering.
The relationship between local structural disorder and phonon scattering is nonlinear.
Atomic-scale descriptors allow the model to distinguish variations in local atomic environments that traditional bulk descriptors overlook.
Capturing local-environment variations will improve the precision of phonon thermal-conductivity predictions.
The proposed model will improve the accuracy of classifying low-phonon-thermal-conductivity alloys by at least 20% relative to traditional models.
Existing empirical and first-principles models rely primarily on averaged bulk properties and simpler structural descriptors.
The approach is applicable to high-entropy alloys having moderate-to-high atomic-size mismatch and stable phase equilibria.
The approach may be less predictive for alloys containing extreme nonequilibrium phases or amorphous regions.
The approach may be less predictive when electronic heat transport dominates phonon conduction.
Model performance may vary with synthesis conditions and uncharacterized defects.
Time-domain thermoreflectance can be used in the proposed benchmark to determine the actual phonon contribution to thermal conductivity.
Failure to achieve at least a 20% classification improvement over traditional models across the benchmark samples would falsify the hypothesis.
